market_holds: Spot about $0.87-0.99 intraday on 2026-11-20 (Yahoo 5-min tape: an 17,959-ADS print at $0.869 at 18:55 UTC; sealed spot $0.99 at 18:09 UTC), down 23.9% over 5 sessions, 51.5% over 20, at a 52-week low and now under $1. The slide is a near-unbroken grind from $2.78 (the 2026-08-27 registered direct price) on very thin volume (~10-30k ADS/day, about $10-30k a day), against XBI -6.1% and IWM -6.7% over 5 sessions, so most of the 5-day move and nearly all of the 20-day move is its own. No option chain and no EDGAR reaction history in the baseline; my own read of Yahoo bars puts the last four report days at +7.7% (2025-11-24), -12.5% (2026-03-23), +6.6% (2026-05-27) and +7.7% (2026-08-31, confounded by the offering), so a usual report-day move of about 8%. No consensus that matters (one sponsored-research analyst). Guide: runway 'into 1H 2027' reiterated at Q2 (cash $13.1M at 2026-06-30, loan about $6.7M). Already public before the print: the 2026-11-18 sale of the 14.4% APHEXDA royalty to Soleus for $5.6M (closing ~11-30, partial loan repayment removing a $4M minimum-cash covenant), and the SNO GLIX1 update of 2026-11-16 (fourth dose cohort enrolling). Positioning: Armistice Capital bought the August deal (480,696 ADS + 868,225 pre-funded + 2.02M warrants at $2.78, resale F-1 effective 2026-10-02) and reported 514,365 ADS, 9.99%, at 2026-09-30 in a 13G signed 2026-11-16. About 810k ADS have traded since 10-01, so the tape is consistent with that holder selling into the market. Market cap is about $5M on ~5.8M ADS-equivalents, against my estimate of ~$12M of cash at 9-30 before the $5.6M royalty proceeds.
view: This is a nano-cap whose price is being set by a seller, not by news. Nothing the company has said since August is bad: it raised $3.75M, sold a royalty for $5.6M of non-dilutive cash and removed a loan covenant, and GLIX1 is enrolling on schedule. Yet the stock has fallen about two-thirds from the deal price on volume that the August buyer's position could fill by itself. That buyer is a fund known for selling deal stock, and it sat at its 9.99% blocker at quarter-end with pre-funded warrants left to exercise. The release on Monday will most likely be routine. It should show cash of roughly $12M at 9-30 against a ~$5M market cap, probably with runway extended or reaffirmed now that the royalty money and covenant relief are in. It may also give an update on the pancreatic interim/futility analysis 'expected in 2026'. A cash-rich, oversold print has bounced on three of the last four report days, which argues for an up-open. But the overhang has absorbed every piece of good news so far: the royalty-sale day traded 295k ADS and closed flat, then fell 8% and about 15% on the next two days. A pop into a seller with stock left will likely fade by 13:00. Neither force is something I can size, so I hold close to a coin, leaning slightly down for the continuing supply. There is also a tail on each side: runway extension or a clean interim (up), or an ADS-ratio change or financing language (down).

recommendation.reason: The price is being driven by a holder liquidating deal stock into a $10-30k-a-day tape, not by the fundamentals the release will report. The release's likely content (cash well above market cap, runway helped by the royalty sale) is already public in substance and did not stop the slide when it was announced. I cannot tell whether the seller is finished, which is the variable that decides the window, so there is no direction I would bet on.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A material new item in the release: a passed pancreatic interim, or a runway pushed well out into 2028 (up); or an ADS-ratio change, a going-concern line or a new financing (down).

self_critique: The case for up is real. The company trades at well under half its cash. On three of the last four report days it rose. A print that restates the cash and extends the runway can draw microcap buyers on a Monday morning after a -24% week. And if Armistice finished selling with Friday's block, the supply is gone and the bounce has no seller in front of it. The case for further down is that the 5-day and 20-day drift is relentless and phase-0 style continuation after deep falls is the base rate. I cannot see the seller's remaining position, so both cases stand and the number stays near 50.
approach_notes: P4/P6 helped: they made me tie the fall to its cause (a named deal holder selling) rather than read the drawdown as either priced bad news or a bargain. The playbook has nothing on supply overhangs from PIPE or registered-direct buyers in nano-caps, which here decide the window more than the release does.
